quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Nighttime is the safest time for cyclists to ride.
questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Bicycles are hard to see at night, even with lights and reflectors. Drivers and cyclists must stay alert at night to avoid crashes.

questions.question: To help others see you as daylight fades, you should use your:
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams when daylight starts to fade. Only use high beams in open areas with no other drivers nearby.

questions.question: A driver turning left must yield to a cyclist coming from the opposite direction.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Yield to oncoming bicycles the same way you would yield to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting and turn only when the way is clear.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: Diamond signs warn drivers of hazards ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
The vehicle next to the broken line may pass.
The vehicle next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass.

questions.question: On a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control, yield to a vehicle approaching from the right.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Turn your head and look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: This sign is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead, such as traffic direction changes, steep grades, or other dangers.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match the traffic speed, signal, and:

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap, speed up to match traffic, and signal. Merge into the gap when safe. Do not expect other drivers to move for you.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line means traffic goes both ways. You can pass, but only if it is safe and will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before going.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before going.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with multiple tracks, do not move until you can see clearly down all tracks. Another train may be approaching even after the first one passes.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see without moving your head. They are on the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: What does a red painted curb mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: A red curb means you cannot stop, stand, or park there.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and be careful as you proceed.

questions.question: At a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, let traffic already in the intersection go first. Be ready to stop. You can go if no other traffic is close.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The bed of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Children age 12 and under are safest in the back seat. Airbags can hurt young children, so they should never sit in front.

questions.question: When you drive faster, your field of vision:

options.text: Makes it easier to see cross traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. At high speeds, you must watch carefully for hazards.

questions.question: You can cross a dashed white line:

options.text: When it is safe to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross them to change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal several times.
Slow down gradually and avoid braking.
Press the brake pedal down hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and avoid braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep straight. Release the accelerator and do not brake hard. Let the vehicle slow on its own. Use brakes gently only if needed. Pull over when safe.
